 :J U D G M E N T:

This Claim Petition is filed by the Petitioner against the Respondents under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act seeking Compensation of 20,00,000/ for the injuries sustained in a Road Traffic accident.

2. The substance of averments made in the Petition is as under:
That on 23082020 at about 1.00 p.m, when the Petitioner being a pedestrian,
waiting to cross the road at the edge of the Peenya 2nd stage main road, very carefully, SCCH 15 3 MVC No.2945/2020 cautiously observing traffic rules and regulations, at that time, one motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA04JW6316 ridden by its rider came in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the Petitioner.
As a result, the Petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries to all over the body.
3. Immediately after the accident, the Petitioner was taken to Jai Maruthi Hospital, wherein the Petitioner took treatment as an inpatient.
He had spent Rs.2,00,000/ amount towards medical and other incidental charges etc.
4. Prior to the date of accident, the Petitioner was hale and healthy and he was working as a Security guard and was earning Rs.18,000/ per month.
The said accident has occurred due to the rash and negligent riding of the offending motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA04JW6316 by its rider.
Therefore, the Respondent No.1 to 3 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the Petitioner.
Hence, this Petition.

5. In pursuance of service of Notice to the Respondents, the Respondent No.1 to 3 had appeared before the Court SCCH 15 4 MVC No.2945/2020 through their respective Counsels and filed their Objection statement to the main Petition.
6. It is to be noted here that as per the Order on I.A No.VIII dated 2.11.23, the claim petition was dismissed against the Respondent No.1 7.

The Respondent No.2 its Objection Statement denied the age, avocation and income of the Petitioner and contended that, the alleged accident is caused due to the negligence on the part of the Petitioner.

Further he contended that the rider of the offending vehicle was holding a valid and Gangaiah vs United India Ins Co Ltd on 13 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/112369169/
2 effective driving license as on the date of accident.

On these grounds, Respondent No.2 has prayed to dismiss the petition against him.
8. The Respondent No.3 in its Objection Statement denied the age, avocation and income of the petitioner and also denied the accident caused by the rider of the offending motor cycle.

It further contended that the rider of the motor cycle was not having valid and effective driving license at the SCCH 15 5 MVC No.2945/2020 time of accident and thereby violated the policy conditions.
On these grounds it has prayed to dismiss the Petition against it.
9. On the rival Pleadings, my learned Predecessor has framed the following Issues:
ISSUES 1.
Whether the Petitioner proves that, the accident occurred due to rash and negligent act of riding of motorcycle bearing No. KA04 JW6316 and as a result, he sustained injuries?
2. Whether the Petitioner proves the age and earnings of the petitioner as stated in the claim petition?
3. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?
If so, how much and from whom?
4. What Order or Award?
10. In order to prove the case of the Petitioner, the Petitioner got examined himself as P.W.1 and got marked 25 SCCH 15 6 MVC No.2945/2020 documents at Ex.P.1 to Ex.P25.
Further, he examined one witness as PW.2 and got marked 2 documents at Ex.12 and 13 and closed his side evidence.
On the other hand, Respondents did not choose to lead any evidence.

11. Having heard the arguments and upon perusal of the depositions, documents exhibited and materials available on record, my answer to the above Issues are as under:
 Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative.
 Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative  Issue No.3 : Partly in the Affirmative  Issue No.4 : As per the Final Order,
 for the following :
 REASONS 12. Issue No.1 : It is the case of the Petitioner that, he had sustained grievous injuries in the Road Traffic Accident that occurred due to the rash and negligent riding of the offending motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA04JW6316 by its rider.

Further, the Petitioner has examined SCCH 15 10 MVC No.2945/2020 Doctor by name Dr. S.A. Somashekhara as P.W.2 and got marked 2 documents at Ex.P.26 and 27.
19.
PW.1 is subjected for cross examination by the learned counsel for the Respondent No.1.

But,
nothing could be elicited to disbelieve the testimony of PW.1.
The Spot mahazar and Spot sketch clearly shows the width of the road is 40 feet and from the spot there is 35 feet towards the Eastern side edge of the road.
Further, the Respondent No.2 and 3 did not choose to lead any oral or documentary evidence to substantiate their Objection Statement contentions.
Hence, the Respondent No.2 and 3 have failed to substantiate their Objection Statement contentions.

Having regard to the facts and circumstances of the case, this Tribunal is of the opinion that the Petitioner has proved the rash and negligent riding of the offending motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA04JW 6316 by its rider and due to the said accident, the Petitioner had sustained grievous injuries.

Accordingly, I answer Issue No.1 in the 'Affirmative'.
SCCH 15 11 MVC No.2945/2020 20. Issue No.2:
As the Petitioner has proved that the accident has occurred due to the rash and negligent riding of the offending vehicle by its rider, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation.
21. In the Petition, the Petitioner has shown his age as 58 years.
The Petitioner has produced the Aadhaar card at Ex.P25, which shows his birth year as 1960.
The accident has taken place on 23.08.2020.
Hence, at the time of accident, the Petitioner was aged about 60 years.
22. Further, the Petitioner has averred that, he was working as a Security Guard and was earning Rs.18,000/ per month.
But, he has not produced any document in this regard.
Therefore, in the absence of income proof, the notional income to be taken at Rs.12,500/ per month for the purpose of assessment of compensation.
23. With this background, the quantum of compensation to which the Petitioner is entitled may be adjudicated.

For the sake of convenience, discussion may be SCCH 15 12 MVC No.2945/2020 had under following heads:
I. COMPENSATION TOWARDS PAIN, SHOCK AND SUFFERING :
24.

The Wound Certificate i.e., Ex.P4 issued by the Medical Officer of the Jai Maruthi hospital,
Bengaluru shows that in the said accident the Petitioner has sustained following injuries i.e.,
1) Open wound with bone protration over lower 1/3rd of right leg with bleed with Xray features suggestive of fracture both bone of right leg.

25. Having regard to the nature of injuries sustained by the Petitioner, I am of the opinion that,
awarding SCCH 15 13 MVC No.2945/2020 compensation of  90,000/ under this head would be just and reasonable.
II. COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF AMENITIES :
26. Bearing in mind the nature of the injuries sustained by the Petitioner, I am of the opinion that awarding compensation of  40,000/ under this head would be just and reasonable.

III. COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF INCOME DURING THE LAID-UP PERIOD:
27.

The Petitioner deposed in his evidence that he had taken treatment at Jai Maruthi Hospital,
Bengaluru.
Upon going through Ex.P.9 & 10  Discharge summaries shows that the Petitioner was admitted as an inpatient in the said hospital from 23.08.2020 to 27.08.2020 and 10.09.2020 to 14.09.2020.
Therefore, while calculating the total period of which the Petitioner was admitted as an inpatient, it comes to 10 days.
28. Having regard to the nature of injuries sustained SCCH 15 14 MVC No.2945/2020 by the Petitioner, I am of the opinion that the laid up period may be considered as three months.

Hence,
the Petitioner is entitled for compensation of 37,500/ under this head (@ 12,500/ per month ).
IV.
COMPENSATION TOWARDS ATTENDANT'S CHARGES, EXTRA DIET & NOURISHMENT AND CONVEYANCE :

29. Admittedly, the Petitioner has sustained injuries and during the laid up period, the Petitioner might have engaged an attendant and also he might have spent some amount towards extra diet and nourishment and for his conveyance.

In the facts and circumstances of the case, awarding compensation of 9,000/ (@ 100/ per day) towards attendants charges, 9,000/ towards extra diet and nourishment and 9,000/ towards conveyance would be just and reasonable.

In all,
the Petitioner is entitled for compensation of 27,000/ under this head.
SCCH 15 15 MVC No.2945/2020 V.COMPENSATION TOWARDS MEDICAL EXPENCES :
30 . The petitioner has stated in his evidence that, he had spent Rs.2,00,000/ towards medical and other incidental charges.
In order to prove this fact, he has produced medical bills at Ex.P.12.
I have gone through the medical bills and the acceptable medical bills comes at Rs.2,52,443/.
Hence, by rounding off the same, the same to be taken at 2,52,500/.
Hence, I am of the opinion that the Petitioner is entitled for 2,52,500/ under this head.

sentences.text: VI. COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF FUTURE EARNINGS / COMPENSATION TOWARDS PERMANENT DISABILITY:
31. The petitioner has stated that due to the injuries sustained by him in the accident, he has suffered permanent disablement and he is not able to do his work as he used to do earlier.
Even in his evidence, P.W.1 has deposed to that effect.

32. Further, the Petitioner got examined one witness SCCH 15 16 MVC No.2945/2020 by name Dr.
S.A. Somashekhara as P.W.2 who has deposed regarding the injuries sustained by the Petitioner in a Road Traffic Accident and the treatment taken by him.
Further, he assessed the whole body disability at 24%.
PW.2 got marked OPD record and Xrays at Ex.P26 and 27.
In the cross examination, PW.2 has deposed that he has not personally treated the Petitioner.
He admitted that two fractures of the right leg was united and Radius fracture of left hand of the petitioner was mal united.
Further he admitted that the condition of the petitioner was improved between the period from discharge and he came near him.
He denied the other suggestions.

Having regard to the medical records placed on record, the evidence of P.W.2 and the nature of the injuries sustained by the Petitioner, I am of the opinion that considering the disability of the Petitioner with respect to the whole body at 10% would be just and proper.
33. As per Sarla Verma's Case (2009 ACJ 1298 SC), the multiplier applicable to the Petitioner is 9.

With multiplier of 9, income of 12,200/ per month and disability of the SCCH 15 17 MVC No.2945/2020 Petitioner with respect to his whole body at 10%, the loss of future income comes to 1,35,000/ (12,500/ x 12 = 1,50,000/, 1,50,000/x 9 x 10/100 = 1,35,000/).
Hence, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation of 1,35,000/ under this head.

TOTAL COMPENSATION TO WHICH THE  PETITIONER IS ENTITLED:
 34.

To sum up, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads :
1. Pain, shock & Suffering  90,000 /
2. Loss of amenities  40,000/
3. Loss of income during the laid up  37,500/ period 4.
Attendant's charges, Extra diet,  27,000/ and conveyance 5.

Medical expenses  2,52,500/
Gangaiah vs United India Ins Co Ltd on 13 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/112369169/
7 6.

Loss of Future Income  1,35,000/ Total Rs.5,82,000/
35.
Thus, totally the Petitioner is awarded compensation SCCH 15 18 MVC No.2945/2020 of Rs.5,82,000/ with costs and simple interest at 6% p.a. from the date of this petition till the date of realization.

36. Regarding Liability: This Court has arrived at the conclusion that the accident has been occurred by the rash and negligent riding on the part of the rider of the offending motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA04JW6316.
There is no dispute about the validity of the Policy at the time of the accident.
It is noted here that the Respondent No.1 was deleted as the policy issued by the Respondent No.1 was Standard own damage policy.
Respondent No.3 is the insurer of the offending vehicle.
Respondent No.2 is the owner of the vehicle.
Therefore, the Respondent No.2 and 3 are jointly and severally liable to satisfy the award amount.
The Respondent No.3, who is liable to indemnify the Respondent No.2, has to pay the compensation amount to the Petitioner.
Accordingly, I answer Issue No.2 and 3 is in the "Partly in the Affirmative".
37. Issue No.4:

In view of my findings on Issues No. 1 SCCH 15 19 MVC No.2945/2020 to 3, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The Claim Petition filed by the U/S 166 of M.V. Act is hereby allowed in part with costs.
The Petitioner is entitled for Compensation of Rs.5,82,000/ along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of the Petition till the date of deposit of Award amount.
The Respondent No.2 and 3 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation amount to the Petitioner.
The Respondent No.3 being the insurer, is directed to deposit the Award amount and interest within 60 days from the date of the Award.

Out of the compensation amount awarded to the Petitioner, 75% of the award amount with accrued interest shall be SCCH 15 20 MVC No.2945/2020 released to the Petitioner by way of E payment and after proper identification.
The remaining 25% award amount shall be deposited as F.D. in the name of the Petitioner in any Nationalized or Scheduled bank for a period of three years.

The Advocate fee is fixed at 1,000/.
Draw Award accordingly.
